Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "Leonie, not Ellis, can you make this into a clear prompt for the accessibility audit note? It was the Maple Quay Interchange walk-through on Tuesday, October 21, 2025, from 7:45 to 10:20 in the morning. The field sheet is by Nia Chen and Omar Bell. Need a neutral account based on the notes, not a verdict on whether the interchange meets a standard. Keep what was seen apart from what somebody reported, and don't turn estimates or gaps in the notes into facts.

The start of the route was a bit mixed up in my notes: stop 14 has a shelter, a bench and a timetable case. At 8:03 and again at 8:16, the printed route 6 schedule was there but the electronic arrivals panel was blank. The notes don't say whether the panel was broken or whether service data was unavailable, so don't choose between those. From the stop toward the crossing, the east sidewalk has a resurfacing fence along it for about 7.4 metres. Nia's tape measurement says the clear width at its narrowest point was 1.16 metres. Don't call this acceptable or unacceptable; there isn't a standard or enough measurement information in these notes to do that. At Pine Avenue the team found a curb ramp on the northeast corner and a tactile panel, with two rows of raised bars missing at the curb edge. They did not measure the ramp slope or the curb lip. The crossing locator tone was audible to the team. On the first signal cycle they did not hear a spoken message, and on the next cycle they did. No signal timing was recorded and the field sheet doesn't explain the difference.

After crossing Pine they used the west entrance. The automatic door button was on the right-hand post; Omar wrote down that it was roughly one metre above the pavement, but that was an estimate, not a tape reading. The door opened when pressed on their visit. In the west concourse the walking route was clear at 8:31. A floor-cleaning sign was beside the wall near the ticket hall; it did not block the route in the team's notes. There are two ticket machines. On the left one the screen was on and the card reader was lit, but the notes don't say they tried to buy a ticket. The right machine had a paper notice over its screen reading “Temporarily unavailable.” The notes don't say how long it had been there or whether the machine was tested. Please keep the exact notice as a quote and don't claim that either machine completed a transaction.

The station attendant was identified in the sheet as Inez. Omar's note says Inez told them, “The lift has been stopping between floors since Monday, but it moved normally this morning.” Keep the wording as reported speech, not as something the team verified for earlier days. At 8:52 the team called the lift from the ticket hall; the doors opened, the car was empty, and they rode to platform 2. The floor indicator changed during the ride and displayed 2 at arrival. The panel had raised buttons and labels, but Braille was not checked. There was no stop or delay noted on this trip. The team did not test the lift at another time or interview passengers, so please don't use the single trip as proof of usual operation or turn Inez's comment into a measured finding.

On platform 2 the yellow edge strip was visible along the area they walked. They wrote that the gap between train and platform was not measured, and no train arrived while they were on that section. A bench was present near the lift landing, with a rubbish bin beside its far end. The notes do not say whether either item affected boarding or the clear route. A sign pointing to the accessible toilet was visible from the ticket hall, but the toilet itself was not visited; a cleaning sign was on its door when seen from the corridor. Don't state that the toilet was open, closed, usable, or unavailable. Please use numbered sections if that helps make the route and observations easy to follow, but don't add a standards assessment, recommendations, or a claim that the team tested anything not listed here.

There are four photographs, labelled in the field sheet: A, stop 14 and the blank arrivals panel; B, the fenced sidewalk beside the measured narrow point; C, the right ticket machine and its notice; and D, the lift indicator showing 2. The notes don't include photographs of the crossing signal, ramp, platform gap, or toilet. No mobile app was tested, no passenger interviews were conducted, and the group did not take signal timings. End the requested note with those limits and the unvisited toilet and unmeasured platform gap as distinct information, rather than adding a summary or a conclusion. The final thing should be an audit note prompt that another writer can use from these observations, not the audit note itself.", "output": "Leonie, not Ellis, please prepare a neutral accessibility audit note for the Maple Quay Interchange walk-through described below. Use only the supplied field observations and reports. Keep observed facts separate from reported speech, estimates, and information that was not collected. Do not give a standards assessment, make recommendations, or claim the team tested anything not listed here.

**Audit details and route**

The walk-through took place on Tuesday, October 21, 2025, from 7:45 to 10:20 in the morning. The field sheet was prepared by Nia Chen and Omar Bell. It was a dry weekday, and resurfacing work was underway on the east side of the station. The route began at eastbound bus stop 14 on Alder Street, crossed at Pine Avenue, then continued through the west concourse and ticket hall to the lift and platform 2.

**Field observations, in route order**

1. **Bus stop and approach to Pine Avenue.** Stop 14 has a shelter, bench, and timetable case. At 8:03 and again at 8:16, the printed route 6 schedule was present, while the electronic arrivals panel was blank. The notes do not establish whether the panel was broken or service data was unavailable. A resurfacing fence ran along the east sidewalk for about 7.4 metres. Nia’s tape measurement recorded a clear width of 1.16 metres at its narrowest point. The notes do not provide a standards assessment or enough measurement information to determine whether that width is acceptable.

2. **Crossing.** At Pine Avenue, the team found a curb ramp on the northeast corner and a tactile panel with two rows of raised bars missing at the curb edge. The ramp slope and curb lip were not measured. The crossing locator tone was audible to the team. They did not hear a spoken message on the first signal cycle, but heard one on the next. No signal timing was recorded, and the field sheet does not explain the difference.

3. **West entrance and ticket hall.** The automatic door button was on the right-hand post. Omar estimated its height at roughly one metre above the pavement; this was not a tape measurement. The door opened when pressed during the visit. At 8:31, the walking route in the west concourse was clear. A floor-cleaning sign beside the wall near the ticket hall was not recorded as blocking the route. There were two ticket machines. The left machine’s screen was on and its card reader was lit, but the team did not record trying to buy a ticket. A paper notice on the right machine read “Temporarily unavailable.” The notes do not say how long the notice had been there or whether that machine was tested. Do not claim that either machine completed a transaction.

4. **Lift.** The field sheet identifies the station attendant as Inez. Omar recorded Inez saying, “The lift has been stopping between floors since Monday, but it moved normally this morning.” Present this as reported speech, not as something the team verified about earlier days. At 8:52, the team called the lift from the ticket hall. The doors opened, the car was empty, and they rode to platform 2. The floor indicator changed during the ride and displayed 2 at arrival. The panel had raised buttons and labels; Braille was not checked. No stop or delay was noted on this trip. The team did not test the lift at another time or interview passengers. Do not treat this single trip as proof of usual operation or turn Inez’s comment into a measured finding.

5. **Platform and toilet sign.** The yellow edge strip was visible along the area the team walked on platform 2. The gap between train and platform was not measured, and no train arrived while they were on that section. A bench was near the lift landing, with a rubbish bin beside its far end. The notes do not state whether either item affected boarding or the clear route. A sign pointing to the accessible toilet was visible from the ticket hall. The toilet itself was not visited; a cleaning sign was on its door when seen from the corridor. Do not state that the toilet was open, closed, usable, or unavailable.

**Photographs and limits**

The field sheet lists four photographs: A, stop 14 and the blank arrivals panel; B, the fenced sidewalk beside the measured narrow point; C, the right ticket machine and its notice; and D, the lift indicator showing 2. There are no photographs of the crossing signal, ramp, platform gap, or toilet. No mobile app was tested, no passenger interviews were conducted, and the team did not take signal timings. End the audit note with these limits, and include the unvisited toilet and unmeasured platform gap as distinct information. Do not add a summary or conclusion."}]
